correctness.rationale: For fixed r>=2, clone each threshold demand and use Hall marriage: disjoint witnesses iff every nonempty J has |union S_i|>=sum k_i. Independent centered Bin(n,p_n) counts converge jointly to N(a_i,1). The overcount B_J=sum_i |S_i|-|union| has expectation binom(|J|,2) n p_n^2+O(np_n^3), variance O(np_n^2), so B_J/s_n concentrates at binom(|J|,2)tau_n when tau_n bounded, uniformly over the finitely many J. Gaussian boundary probabilities vanish, yielding the exact order-statistic Hall polytope and crossover p_n~n^(-1/3). If tau_n diverges, a pair intersection scaled by s_n diverges while binomial margins stay tight, so success tends to zero. The small tau^2 pair-triangle law and large tau Gaussian total-sum tail follow by finite inclusion-exclusion and conditional Gaussian concentration. The claims assume fixed r and offsets and np_n->infty; finite simulations are not the proof.
